sentence: This project studies how the microbiome makes bile acids joined to amino acids and how these molecules change inflammatory signaling in disease models.
This project runs rapid autopsies on patients who die of cancer to study how tumors change and become resistant to drugs.
This project studies how skeletal muscle stays healthy and what muscle stem cells do in keeping it that way.
This project works where nanotechnology, cancer biology and oncology meet, aiming at tools to detect, diagnose, treat and prevent cancer.
This project studies how a poorly understood molecule holds back the immune response against ovarian cancer.
This project studies how a gene regulator affects why dopamine neurons in the midbrain are lost in Parkinson's disease.
This project studies how a protein in the membrane around the cell nucleus drives liver tumors in people with long-term liver disease.
This project tries to find the cell and molecule signals that cause muscle scarring after spinal cord injury and tests ways to target it.
This project designs a gene delivery carrier that is not viral to bring a brain protein into the brain of mice with Alzheimer's disease.
This project looks for missed chances to diagnose pancreatic cancer sooner and builds electronic tools that flag patients at high risk.
This project builds a portable sensor kit that uses fluorescence, solid phase extraction membranes and artificial intelligence to detect PFAS quickly on site.
This project studies blood immune cells and brain function in people with lupus who are in long remission, and looks for signs of relapse.
This project studies how stress and a hormone called progesterone relate to women returning to cannabis use after giving birth.
This project studies whether a natural steroid hormone helps learning and memory in mice and how it relates to thinking skills in aging people.
This project builds a message system guided by machine learning that helps people with alcohol use disorder stay engaged with digital therapy.
This project develops a course that teaches bioinformatics using the real-world problem of antibiotic resistance.
This project tries to make microbes produce more rare anticancer molecules, then studies their structures and designs variants that work better.
This project studies how blocking a protein on T cells, alone or with another drug, changes the immune response to head and neck cancer.
This project uses zebrafish to study how mutations in RNA Polymerase III cause a rare childhood brain disorder and to screen compounds that might help.
This project uses genetic engineering of pigs to overcome molecular differences that cause pig organs to fail when transplanted into primates.
